1.why: The UI uses a clean sans-serif typeface with clear letter spacing, comfortable line height, and ample padding inside cards.

2.why: Instructions use sentence case with no italics, no all-caps, and only short single-sentence blocks.

3.why: Content is presented in a single-column card layout that remains readable when narrowed, though the provided screenshots are wide desktop views.

4.why: Every instruction is one short plain-language sentence such as “Generate backup codes and store them safely.”

5.why: No example or placeholder format (e.g., 123456) is shown for the authenticator code input; only the label and a six-digit mention appear.

6.why: No screen requires reading a long instructional paragraph; all prompts are brief and the logs are optional reference.

7.why: The Base32 secret and recovery codes are rendered as ordinary selectable text that can be copied, although no explicit copy button is present.

8.why: Only a manual Base32 secret is offered; no QR code or equivalent scannable alternative appears on any screen.

9.why: Standard email and telephone inputs are used that normally allow browser autofill, but no password-manager hooks or autocomplete attributes are visible.

10.why: Each page has a clear heading naming the current step and a prominent blue button for the primary action, though no step-progress indicator exists.

11.why: Screens focus on one main task at a time; secondary actions such as Log out or Regenerate remain visually subordinate.

12.why: The final “MFA is active” message and log entries confirm outcomes, yet intermediate screens rarely state plainly what just happened and what follows.

13.why: Recovery codes can be regenerated and re-viewed later without penalty; no lock-outs or forced restarts are shown.

14.why: No error states appear in the screenshots, so it is impossible to confirm whether messages explain problems without blame.

15.why: No countdown timers or expiration warnings are displayed on any step for reading or code entry.
